answer: A reputation stake that decays like a tide offers one concrete defence. Each agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can trade, and the deposit is slashed when peers prove it spawned fake identities. Like saffron grown on a narrow terrace, honest history is slow and costly to cultivate but quick to lose: a Sybil farmer must pay the deposit for every sock puppet and risks losing all of them at once, while a single honest agent pays once and keeps trading.
